## generic_dense_field_gen3

**No issue found in the checked scope.** Current generator SHA-256: `8d9c79b7259d2306950f1bed733426e35f7b2e883f1e2656b433a6f2efd61638`.

A fresh deterministic probe generated 50 tasks per difficulty band (150 tasks total), covering 700 pair instances and 700 cyclic two-demo/one-query windows. All 700 inputs were unique. Every input satisfied all five declared witnesses; each of the four declared rivals (`take_right_half`, `take_center_half`, `mirror_left_half`, and `emit_modal_color_block`) disagreed with the answer on 700/700 pairs; every cyclic lesson passed `lesson_identifiable` and `self_check_task`.

Evidence: `checks/audit/generic_dense_field_gen3/probe.json`. This is a finite declared-rival Python audit, not proof against every possible shortcut; no new Racket counterexample is claimed. The interrupted aggregate audit battery is retained separately under `checks/audit-batteries/generic_dense_field_gen3-before/` and had passed lint and self-check before the outer command cap stopped it.

## generic_dense_field_gen3

No issue found after checking 300 generated tasks: 100 each for easy, medium, and hard.

The audit covered all generated train/test pairs: 400 unique easy inputs, 400 unique medium inputs, and 600 unique hard inputs. `self_check_task` returned no finding. Every pair disagreed with all four declared rivals (`take_right_half`, `take_center_half`, `mirror_left_half`, and `emit_modal_color_block`). Each band exercised every declared dimension profile. Replaying the same hard seed was deterministic, and generation left Python's global random state unchanged.

This does not prove the absence of every imaginable shortcut, but I found no concrete counterexample or surviving plausible rival within the declared grammar.

Evidence: `checks/audit_probes.log`.
